questions.question: If x% of 190 is 15 less than (x + 10)% of 180, then (x + 30)% of 90 is what per cent more than x% of 150?
questions.solution:

⇒ xover100 × 190 + 15 = (x + 10)over100 × 180

⇒ 190x + 1500 = 180x + 1800

⇒ 10x = 300

⇒ x = 30 

Substituting the value of x in the equation-

(x + 30)% of 90

questions.question: A customer paid Rs. 306 for an item after availing successive discounts of 10% and 15%. What is the marked price of the item (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Effective discount rate = d1 + d2 - d₁ × d₂ over 100

Where “d1” and “d2” are successive discount rates.

MP = SPover(100 - D) × 100, where

MP = Marked price

SP = Selling Price

D = Discount %

Calculated:

Effective discount = 10 + 15 - 10 × 15 over 100 = 23.5%

Let the marked price be 100

⇒ SP = 100 - 23.5 = 76.5

Actual marked price = 306over 76.5 × 100 = Rs 400

∴ The marked price is Rs 400.

questions.question: The average weight of 18 boxes in a boat is increased by 2.5 kg when one of the boxes weighing 75 kg is replaced by a new box. The weight (in kg) of the new box is:
questions.solution:
Formula:

Average weight = Total weight of boxes ÷ Total number of boxes 

Calculation:

Let the average weight be "a".

Total weight of boxes = 18 × a = 18a

Let the weight of new box be "y".

Acccording to the question-

⇒ 18a - 75 + y = 18 × (a + 2.5) 

⇒ 18a - 75 + y = 18a + 45

⇒ y = 120 kg

The weight of new box is 120 kg.

questions.question: A earns Rs. 2,250 in a day if he works for 8 hours a day. B earns Rs. 3,750 per day if he works for 6 hours a day. The ratio of the per hour wages of A to that of B is:
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Per hour wage = Total wage ÷ Total hours

**Calculation:**

Per hour wage of A = Rs 2250 ÷ 8 = 2250over8

Per hour wage of B = 3750over6 

Ratio of wages = {2250over8}over{3750over6} = 2250over8 × 6over3750 = 9 : 20

∴ **The ratio is 9 : 20.**

Time period for daughter = 3 years

Rate = 20%

Concept used:

We would equate the amount accrued to the son as well as the daughter at the end of their time period to find the principal amount for the son. 

Formula used:

A = P × (1+ {r over 100})t 

Where A = Amount after time "t".

P = Principal, r = Rate 

Calculation:

⇒ Amount for the daughter = 10,25,000 - P

Amount for the son at the end of 5 years = P × (1 + 20over 100)5

Amount for the daughter at the end of 3 years = (10,25,000 - P) × (1 + 20over 100)3

Now, According to Question

⇒ 36Pover 25 = 10,25,000 - P

⇒ 36P = 25,625,000 - 25P

⇒ 61P = 25,625,000

⇒ P = 25,625,000over 61 = Rs 4,20,082

∴ Rs **4,20,082** was deposited in the name of her son.

questions.question: A, B and C can do one-third of a work in 15 days, 30 days and 10 days, respectively. A started the work. C joined him after 1 day and B joined them after 3 days of the beginning. For how many days did C work?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Efficiency = Time taken for total work ÷ Time taken to complete work individually

**Calculation:**

According to the question-

A can do one-third of a work in 15 days.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete the work = 15over {1over3} = 45 days

B can do one-third of a work in 30 days.

⇒ Time taken by B to complete the work = 30over {1over3} = 90 days

C can do one-third of a work in 10 days.

⇒ Time taken by C to complete the work = 10over {1over3} = 30 days

LCM of 3, 30, 45 and 90 = 90

Taking the total work to be 90 units.

Efficiency of A = 90 units ÷ 45 = 2 units/day

Efficiency of B = 90 units ÷ 90 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of C = 90 units ÷ 30 = 3 units/day

According to the question-

Work done on 1st day = 2 units

Work done on 2nd and 3rd day = (3 + 2) × 2 = 10 units

Total work done till 3rd day = 10 + 2 = 12 units

Remaining = 90 - 12 = 78 units

Work done by A, B, and C in one day = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 units

Days C will work = 78 ÷ 6 = 13 days

Total days C worked = 13 + 2 = 15 days.

∴ **The total days C worked is 15 days.**

questions.question: A 70 cm wide path is made around a circular garden having a diameter of 14 metres. What is the area of the path (in m²)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a circular path of width w outside a circle of radius r is given by π × w × (2r + w).

Given width w = 70 cm = 0.7 m and inner radius r = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m.

⇒ Area = π × 0.7 × (2 × 7 + 0.7)

⇒ Area = π × 0.7 × 14.7 = 10.29 π

**∴ The correct answer is 10.29 π m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circular garden = 14 m

Width of the path (w) = 70 cm = 0.7 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/73cdcdbcc521b0b75a4f1424617c35b253d93615e7ede3ef40474ca30c758703.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of circular ring = π × (R² − r²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius of the inner garden (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 m

⇒ Radius of the outer circle (R) = 7 + 0.7 = 7.7 m

⇒ Area of the path = π × (7.7² − 7²)

⇒ Area of the path = π × (7.7 − 7) × (7.7 + 7)

⇒ Area of the path = π × 0.7 × 14.7

⇒ Area of the path = 10.29 π m²

**∴ The correct answer is 10.29 π m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Circular Ring

The area enclosed between two concentric circles of radii R and r (where R > r) is given by π(R² − r²).

Path Inside a Circle

If a path of width w is constructed inside a circular garden of radius R, the area of the path becomes π × w × (2R − w).

Length of Arc and Area of Sector

For a circle of radius r, length of an arc subtending angle θ is (θ÷360) × 2πr, and the area of the sector is (θ÷360) × πr².

questions.question: A car covers the first 80 km of its journey at a speed of 40 km/h. The driver makes a stop at the tea-stall for 30 minutes and then continues his journey at a speed of 60 km/h for 4 hours. What is his average speed (in km/h, correct to 1 decimal place)?
questions.solution:

Average speed = Total distance covered ÷ total time taken

Distance covered = Speed × time

**Calculation:**

Total distance covered = 80 km + (60 × 4) km

Total distance covered = 80 km + 240 km = 320 km

Total time taken =​​​​80over40 hrs + 1over2 hrs + 4 hrs = 13over2 hrs.

∴ Average speed = 320 ÷ 13over2 = 320 × 2over13 = 49.2 km/h

**The average speed is 49.2 km/h.**

questions.solution:

Discount (d1) = 18%

Discount (d2) = 12%

Discount (d3) = 10%

Effective discount = d1 + d2 - d₁ × d₂ over 100

Where “d1” and “d2” are successive discounts offered.

Calculation:

Effective discount = 18 + 12 - 18 × 12 over 100 = 30 - 2.16 = 27.84

Final discount = 27.84 + 10 - 27.84 × 10over 100 = 37.84 - 2.784 = 35.056%

questions.question: The average weight of a class of 20 students is 44 kg. A new student joins the class the average weight decreases by 300 gm. What is the weight of the new student (in kg)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of new student = Old Average − (New Total Students × Decrease in Average)

Decrease in Average = 300 gm = 0.3 kg

New Total Students = 20 + 1 = 21

Weight = 44 − (21 × 0.3)

Weight = 44 − 6.3 = 37.7 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students initially (n₁) = 20

Initial average weight (A₁) = 44 kg

Decrease in average = 300 gm = 0.3 kg

**Formula:**

Total Weight = Number of students × Average Weight

 
 Initial Group (20)
 Avg = 44 kg
 
 Final Group (21)
 Avg = 43.7 kg
 

 New student weight = Total₂₁ − Total₂₀
 Result: 917.7 − 880 = 37.7 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of 20 students = 20 × 44 = 880 kg

⇒ New average weight = 44 − 0.3 = 43.7 kg

⇒ New total number of students = 21

⇒ Total weight of 21 students = 21 × 43.7 = 917.7 kg

⇒ Weight of the new student = 917.7 − 880 = 37.7 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 37.7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Adding a Member

If the average increases, the new member's weight = Old Average + (New Total × Increase). If it decreases, use − instead of +.

Net Deviation Principle

The sum of deviations from the average is always zero. New student weight = Old Average + Total Members × Change in Average.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are uniform: 1 kg = 1000 gm. Thus, 300 gm = 300/1000 = 0.3 kg.</p

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed towards each other at speeds 88 km/h and 75 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 65 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Concept:**

The time remains constant for the trains while the distance varies. We would use this concept to solve the question.

**Calculation:**

Let the time after which the trains meet be "t".

Distance traveled by 1st train during "t" = 88 × t

Distance traveled by 2nd train during "t" = 75 × t

According to the question-

⇒ 88t - 75t = 65 km

⇒ 13t = 65 km

∴ t = 5 hrs

Distance between the two station = (88 + 75) × 5 = 163 × 5 = 815 km

∴ **The distance between the stations is 815 km.**

questions.question: Find the number nearest to 51462, that is divisible by 8.
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

The nearest number to 51462 which is completely divisible by 8 can be found by dividing 51462 by 8 and checking for the remainder. The next multiple is taken if the remainder is greater than half the divisor. Elsewise, the previous multiple is taken as the answer.

**Calculation:**

According to the question-

⇒ Divisor = 8

on dividing 51462 by 8, we get-

⇒ Dividend = 6432

⇒ Remainder = 6

Since, Remainder is greater than half the divisor i.e., 8, the Next multiple is taken.

∴ Next multiple = 6433 × 8 = 51,464

**The answer is 51,464.**

Expected gain = 1.2 × Rs 50 = Rs 60.

Let the selling price of remaining wheat be "a"

⇒ 200a = 39000 - (15500 + 7600)

⇒ a = 15,900 ÷ 200 = 79.5

∴ **The cost of remaining wheat should be Rs 79.5 per kg.**
